thread:
Jordan (PM): Heads-up — Support got a high-priority request from FinLedger. They want streaming function/tool-calls that emit structured reconciliation events in real time to drive a live UI. Currently their client chokes on partial JSON frames. Asking: scope + priority + minimal launch criteria.
Maya (Support): Ticket summary: https://support.redwood/FL-4821 - user sees broken JSON when we stream fncall outputs. They expect schema: {account_id, txn_id, amount, status}. Failing with partial frames when we stream incremental fields. Customer says it's blocking their launch next month.
Tom (Sales): FinLedger is on a POC and will pay for Dedicated if we can guarantee low-latency streaming + schema stability. They're sensitive to token costs but OK with a commitment.
Ravi (Eng-runtime): Quick notes from runtime POV: streaming fncalls + structured output touches batching, KV cache flush, and our frame emitter. Two main failure modes: (1) we emit partial JSON across frames and some clients attempt JSON.parse on each frame -> broken, (2) backpressure + connection drop = incomplete final object.
Lina (Eng-ML): From model side we can emit discrete events if guided by a strict prompt/template, but we need support for "resume tokens" or an explicit end-of-object marker so clients can concat safely. Also recommending we surface schema validation hooks in the API so users can fail fast.
Jordan (PM): Proposal for minimal viable scope (MVS):
- Server-side: add a streaming framing protocol that guarantees one of: complete-object-per-frame OR newline-delimited JSON objects (NDJSON) + final "eof" marker.
- API: flag streaming_schema=true, and an optional schema_id for server-side validation.
- SDKs: helper that consumes frames and emits only validated objects.
- Telemetry: emit metrics for partial-frame count, dropped connections, avg time-to-first-object.
Goal: ship MVS to Hosted first, then Dedicated.
Ravi (Eng-runtime): Implementation concerns: PLAT-queue batching might need to hold partial tokens until object close -> increases memory for long-lived streams. Also need to decide whether to compress frames (gzip) which breaks streaming semantics for many browsers.
Maya (Support): Customer-side workaround: they wrapped frames and reassembled, but it's fragile — depends on consistent newline separators which we don't guarantee today.
Ava (Product): Launch criteria suggestion:
- End-to-end: example app that streams a reconciliation event every 200ms for 5k events without malformed JSON.
- SDKs: reference client for Node and browser that exposes onObject(obj) and handles reconnections transparently.
- Docs: clear migration guide for existing streaming chat/completions users.
- Telemetry & SLA: baseline metrics captured and a plan for dedicated rollout and opt-in quantization (if cost becomes an issue).
Jordan (PM): Prioritization ask: is this P1 for the API team? FinLedger is a close revenue opportunity and the bug blocks them. Alternatives: defer to Dedicated-only (quicker) or provide a beta with caveats. Thoughts?
Ravi (Eng-runtime): P1 if we own the framing protocol here. If we punt to Dedicated-only, we can ship a more controlled runtime quicker. For Hosted we need more QA and perf tuning.
Lina (Eng-ML): We can provide a prompt pattern and a model-side hard marker (<END_OBJ>) to make stream boundaries explicit. That reduces runtime holding but requires evals to ensure models respect it.
Tom (Sales): If Dedicated-only reduces ETA by 6 weeks, customer will sign. But they'd prefer Hosted ultimately.
Ava (Product): Risk register: client compatibility (parsing libs), perf (increased memory), rollout complexity (hosted->dedicated->private). Mitigation: NDJSON default + opt-in strict schema validation.
triage-bot: tag:customer-request,priority:high,owner:unassigned
Jordan (PM): Next steps:
1) Decision: ship Dedicated-beta (narrow) vs Hosted-MVS (broad). -> action: @Ravi + @Lina to estimate effort (EOD Wednesday).
2) Support to draft public-facing caveats and a ticket template for structured-streaming bugs. -> @Maya
3) Sales to confirm commercial commitment window -> @Tom
4) Product to draft launch criteria + telemetry spec -> @Ava
Ravi (Eng-runtime): I'll take the Dedicated-beta estimate — will post numbers tomorrow.
Lina (Eng-ML): I'll own prompt pattern + simple model eval.
Maya (Support): Drafting the ticket template now. Will link sample client logs.
Tom (Sales): I'll ping FinLedger for timeline confirmation.
Ava (Product): I'll draft the launch criteria doc and minimal SDK contract.
Jordan (PM): Thanks all. We'll reconvene after estimates. :thumbsup:
